pathway.title: Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is high and rising on every measure, and the headline cover ratio flatters. Total debt was 3.29x reported EBITDA at FY2024, 5.97x at FY2025 and 8.83x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, with net leverage at 7.47x, because borrowing for turbines and acquisitions has run ahead of earnings. Cash interest cover of 21.08x is flattered by interest capitalised on assets under construction and by a first coupon on the 2031 senior notes that falls after the period; on total interest cost the nine-month cover is 3.55x, and full-year coupons on the four note issues alone are USD 179.6 million, which last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 294.5 million covers 1.64 times before the Stateline loan, equipment financing and revolver costs. Pro forma net leverage for the October 2026 senior notes is not established, and after the later Stateline draw of USD 25.0 million it is 7.56x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation A11; calculation A12

- Free cash flow is deeply negative and capital markets, not operations, finance the gap. Operating cash flow of USD 573.9 million over the last twelve months includes customer prepayments, with deferred revenue adding USD 207.2 million and contract liabilities USD 77.5 million in the first nine months of 2026, against capital expenditure of USD 1,636.9 million, so free cash flow was negative USD 1,062.9 million. Power equipment purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million remain, USD 569.1 million of them in the rest of 2026, and about USD 1 billion of capital spend is still planned for 2026; the prepayments are interest-free funding that unwinds as leases run, so they do not remove the need for new borrowing. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation F24

- Contracted rent gives revenue visibility, but lease start dates decide when it arrives. Future lease payments of USD 6,751.5 million are disclosed, including leases not yet started, with USD 801.0 million due in 2027 and 50.31% falling after 2030, and 2026 brought several large contracts with affiliates of investment-grade technology companies. No Stateline lease had started by September 30, 2026, the first-signed Hatchbo contract could be ended on 30 days notice for a payment of 50% of remaining rent, and the credit agreement can force repayment or cut borrowing if certain material contracts end early, so a delay or an exit hits liquidity as well as revenue. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 138; calculation A15

- Diversification is weak on customers, segment and supplier, and growth is arriving with a thinner margin. One customer was 59% of third-quarter revenue and 67% of receivables, a single data-center customer was 88% of Power Solutions revenue in FY2025, Power Solutions made 75% of revenue and 80% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in nine months, and one supplier was 38% of purchases. Power Solutions Adjusted EBITDA was 59% of its own revenue in nine months 2025 and 52% in nine months 2026. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 11

- Liquidity is adequate for the near term but fell quickly, and the maturity wall is distant. Cash of USD 399.5 million and undrawn revolver of USD 525.0 million gave USD 924.5 million at September 30, 2026, down USD 474.6 million in the quarter from USD 1,399.1 million and covering purchase commitments 0.70 times; the effect on cash of the October 2026 senior notes, with net proceeds of about USD 1.23 billion, is not established. Only USD 209.8 million of principal falls due in 2030 and 85.34% falls due in 2031 or later, and the 2030 convertible notes are in the money, so refinancing is a 2031 question that depends on markets staying open while contracts start. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation A2; calculation A3; calculation A4; calculation A5; calculation A13

- Financial policy is growth-first and governance risk is medium. The filings describe no controlling holder and no sponsor extraction: dividends were USD 22.8 million in nine months, 1.65% of capital expenditure, and payments to a company owned by the Chairman were USD 0.8 million, but the company chose debt and shares over deleveraging to fund USD 1,382.4 million of capital expenditure and three acquisitions. Class B holders held about 22% of votes in early 2026, controls at the two acquired services businesses are not yet tested, and the revolver limits net leverage to 5.25x while reported total debt to EBITDA is 8.83x, so the covenant definitions must differ from the reported figures and headroom is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation A19

runs.text: A large contracted lease book supports revenue visibility. Future lease payments of USD 6,751.5 million, including leases not yet started, with USD 801.0 million due in 2027 and 50.31% after 2030, are fixed for the lease term, and the Hatchbo and April 2026 contracts are with affiliates of investment-grade technology companies, so once equipment starts earning, long fixed rent should support debt service; the strength depends on start dates and on termination terms that were not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; calculation A15

Demonstrated access to bond, convertible and revolver markets limits near-term refinancing risk. The company issued USD 1.3 billion of senior notes in May and USD 1.25 billion in October 2026 and raised the revolver to USD 850.0 million, and only USD 209.8 million of principal falls due in 2030, so the debt maturity wall sits in 2031 and later; access is proven only in an open market and for a growth story still to be delivered. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; calculation A13

Financial policy takes little cash out and the filings describe no controlling holder. Dividends of USD 22.8 million and payments of USD 0.8 million to an entity of the Chairman are small against capital expenditure of USD 1,382.4 million, and the filings describe no waiver, exchange offer or priming transaction, so leakage to shareholders is a minor credit risk on current evidence. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; calculation A19

High and rising leverage is the main weakness. Total debt reached 2.44 times its year-end 2025 level, USD 2,599.8 million, which is 8.83x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, and annual coupons on the four note issues of USD 179.6 million take much of that EBITDA, so earnings from new leases must arrive for coverage to hold. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation A1; calculation A11; calculation A12

Negative free cash flow makes the company dependent on outside funding. Operating cash flow of USD 573.9 million, helped by customer prepayments, covered about a third of capital expenditure of USD 1,636.9 million over the last twelve months, and purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million remain. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 60

Concentration leaves the credit exposed to one counterparty and one segment. One customer was 59% of revenue and 67% of receivables, Power Solutions was 75% of revenue, and the first-signed Hatchbo contract could be ended on 30 days notice, and if it counts as a material contract under the credit agreement, whose definition was not supplied, its early end could force repayment or reduce borrowing. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 138

Integration and execution risk has risen with three acquisitions in 2026. GESA and Omega, added on July 1 and September 1, are outside the management assessment of internal control, Omega works mainly under fixed-price contracts, and a new Chief Accounting Officer starts on November 12, 2026, so earnings and reporting could be more volatile than the legacy leasing business. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 16–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 81–84

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The 2026 transactions were three acquisitions and two senior note issues. Genco, a purchase of leased gas turbines completed on March 16, 2026, cost USD 483.2 million, paid partly with stock issued of USD 238.4 million and financed partly by a USD 300.0 million bridge loan that the May notes repaid; the later report is net of USD 1.1 million recovered from escrow, so the earlier USD 484.3 million is superseded. GESA, completed on July 1, 2026 for USD 263.1 million, included shares of USD 211.5 million and added goodwill of USD 169.5 million; Omega, completed on September 1, 2026 for USD 275.2 million, included shares of USD 178.7 million and added goodwill of USD 110.9 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-03-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation A5

The USD 1.3 billion of senior notes due 2031, issued on May 12, 2026, raised net proceeds of USD 1.28 billion and repaid USD 463.9 million of term loans; a USD 650.0 million secured revolver signed the same day was undrawn at September 30, 2026 with USD 125.0 million of letters of credit, and was raised to USD 850.0 million on October 1, 2026. Earlier funding included USD 155.0 million and USD 747.5 million of convertible senior notes, and a Stateline term loan of up to USD 550.0 million, of which USD 408.2 million was drawn at September 30, 2026 without recourse to the company. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 42–48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 65

The USD 1.25 billion of senior notes due 2032, issued on October 1, 2026 after the balance sheet date, raised net proceeds of about USD 1.23 billion for general corporate purposes and growth capital expenditure, so no figure at September 30, 2026 includes them or the further large contract signed on October 29, 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65

fields.value: Financial foundation for Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. (issuer sei-1697500), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is normalised statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the five supplied SEC filings, in US dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage has risen from 3.29x at FY2024 to 8.83x on last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 30, 2026 because debt-funded growth capital expenditure and part-period acquisitions are running ahead of earnings, so creditors depend on contracted leases commencing as planned.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C24; calculation C30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt at carrying value, including convertible notes, was USD 2,599.8 million at September 30, 2026 against cash of USD 399.5 million, and the USD 1.25 billion of senior notes issued on October 1, 2026 sits outside every statement. Reported EBITDA is after USD 57.5 million of losses on debt extinguishment over the last twelve months; excluding them leverage is 7.39x. Interest cover of 21.08x on cash interest paid flatters, because that cash figure is net of capitalised interest and the first coupon on the 2031 senior notes is payable only on November 15, 2026; interest cost incurred was USD 76.7 million in 9M 2026 against USD 11.2 million paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C57; calculation C58; calculation C59; calculation C34; calculation C32; calculation C61; calculation C60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt at carrying value rose from USD 315.730 million at FY2024 to USD 1,064.460 million at FY2025 and USD 2,599.801 million at September 30, 2026, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 95.949 million to USD 178.220 million for FY2025 and USD 294.488 million for the last twelve months. Debt has grown faster than earnings because the 2025 convertible notes and the May 2026 senior notes fund turbine purchases and acquisitions before the leased equipment earns revenue, so reported leverage moved from 3.29x to 5.97x and then 8.83x. Creditors are therefore exposed to the pace at which new capacity commences rather than to current earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C18; calculation C30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 79

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cover on cash interest paid was 8.37x in FY2024, 7.95x in FY2025 and 21.08x over the last twelve months, but the latest figure is flattered: cash interest of USD 13.971 million is after interest capitalised on assets under construction and before the first coupon on the 2031 senior notes. On interest expense the cover is 6.04x, and on total interest cost incurred in 9M 2026 it is 3.55x, the figure closest to the 3.00x minimum in the revolving credit facility although that covenant uses a definition the filing does not print. Cover on cash interest is likely to fall once full coupons on the 2031 and 2032 senior notes are paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C26; calculation C29; calculation C32; calculation C41; calculation C42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow of USD 573.941 million over the last twelve months includes customer prepayments, with deferred revenue adding USD 207.248 million and contract liabilities USD 77.546 million in 9M 2026, which fund operations without interest and are not earnings. Capital expenditure of USD 1,636.870 million is far above operating cash flow, so free cash flow was a negative USD 1,062.929 million and the gap was financed by borrowing and equity issuance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 38

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 399.460 million plus revolver availability of USD 525.0 million, after USD 125.0 million of letters of credit, gives USD 924.460 million at September 30, 2026 against purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million, before the net proceeds of the October 2026 senior notes. Those proceeds, not operating cash flow, are the main source for the roughly USD 1 billion of capital expenditure still planned for 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three definition choices move the results: reported EBITDA carries USD 57.535 million of losses on debt extinguishment, so leverage is 8.83x against 7.39x without them; cash interest paid is net of capitalised interest; and consolidated debt includes the non-recourse Stateline term loan of USD 408.2 million. The December 31, 2024 balance sheet differs by USD 7.577 million between the two annual reports, which affects neither equity nor the debt figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Events after the balance sheet are kept out of period figures: the USD 1.25 billion senior notes, the USD 200.0 million increase in revolving commitments and the USD 25.0 million Stateline draw. Pro forma net debt is established only for the Stateline draw, at USD 2,225.341 million or 7.56x, because the net proceeds of the senior notes are stated only approximately and no pro forma balance sheet or EBITDA is printed. The missing pro forma EBITDA for the 2026 acquisitions and the unprinted covenant EBITDA are the gaps that most restrict any run-rate or headroom conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, transaction, ownership and governance facts for Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. (issuer sei-1697500), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is the five supplied SEC filings, in US dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Solaris has become a customer-concentrated power-leasing and services business whose growth is funded by acquisitions and debt, so creditors depend on a few data-center contracts starting on schedule and on integrating the services businesses it bought in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Power Solutions made 75% of revenue and 80% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in the first nine months of 2026, one customer was 59% of third-quarter revenue and 67% of receivables, and no Stateline lease had started by September 30, 2026. Capital expenditure was USD 1,382.4 million in the period and the company sold USD 1.3 billion of senior notes in May and USD 1.25 billion in October 2026. The filings describe no controlling holder, and sponsor and governance risk is medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit is now mainly a power-leasing and services business, and its margin is thinning as the mix shifts. Power Solutions was 12% of revenue in FY2024, 54% in FY2025 and 75% in the first nine months of 2026, and its share of segment Adjusted EBITDA went from 22% to 68% to 80%. Its Adjusted EBITDA was 59% of its own revenue in the first nine months of 2025 and 52% in the same period of 2026, which fits the addition of services and construction businesses, though the filings do not split margin by business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation A10; calculation A12; calculation A16; calculation A17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is the dominant operating risk, and the documents do not show how well it is protected. One customer was 59% of third-quarter revenue and 67% of receivables at September 30, 2026, and one data-center customer was 88% of Power Solutions revenue in FY2025. No Stateline lease had started by September 30, 2026 although the 2025 annual report expected revenue from that arrangement in 2026, and the USD 6,751.5 million of disclosed future lease payments includes leases that have not started. The first-signed Hatchbo contract let the customer end it on 30 days notice for a payment of 50% of remaining rent; a July 2026 amendment extended the tenor to up to 18 years, but the filings do not say whether the termination right remains. The credit agreement can force repayment or cut borrowing if certain Material Contracts end early, so a termination right matters for liquidity as well as revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 138

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisitions have changed the scale and risk of the company faster than the reporting can show. Reported nine-month revenue was USD 756.7 million, while the filing shows pro forma revenue of USD 1,249.4 million with GESA and Omega for the whole period, and no pro forma EBITDA or debt is printed. Employees rose to at least 4.49 times the year-end 2025 level, and the construction business Omega brought works predominantly under fixed-price contracts; GESA and Omega, 26% and 17% of third-quarter revenue, sit outside the management assessment of internal control, and a new Chief Accounting Officer starts on November 12, 2026.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 81–84; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation A2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisition funding is shared between shares, cash and debt, which limits but does not remove the leverage added. Genco cost USD 483.2 million, GESA USD 263.1 million and Omega USD 275.2 million, with stock issued of USD 238.4 million, USD 211.5 million and USD 178.7 million, and Class A shares outstanding grew 30.78% between year-end 2025 and September 30, 2026. Debt followed: USD 1.3 billion of senior notes in May 2026 repaid the bridge and assumed term loans, USD 1.25 billion more was raised on October 1, 2026 after the balance sheet date, and capital expenditure of USD 1,382.4 million in nine months is to be followed by about USD 1 billion in the rest of 2026, with power equipment purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million outstanding at September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings describe no controlling holder and insiders take little cash, but a minority control block and a corporate-opportunity waiver keep influence with a few holders. Class B holders held about 22% of combined economic interest and voting power in early 2026, and Class B shares were 13.39% of all shares at September 30, 2026 against 22.47% at year-end 2025. Related-party payments were USD 0.8 million, dividends USD 22.8 million, distributions to other Solaris LLC unitholders USD 4.9 million and Tax Receivable Agreement payments USD 1.7 million against a liability of USD 109.2 million, and no shares were bought under the repurchase programme in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance is a medium risk rather than a high one, because the filings describe no extraction, waiver or creditor-adverse transaction, but legal capacity for distributions and debt is untested. The auditor gave unqualified opinions on the 2025 statements and on internal control, and the filings state compliance with the credit agreement at September 30, 2026; the agreement itself and its ratios were not supplied, so headroom cannot be measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a cautious view is that the largest customers are affiliates of investment-grade technology companies, 2026 added further large contracts in February, April and October, USD 6,751.5 million of future lease payments is disclosed, shares paid for much of each 2026 acquisition, and the company held USD 399.5 million of cash and USD 525.0 million of undrawn revolver availability at September 30, 2026, before the USD 1.25 billion issue. The view would improve if the Stateline leases start and the Hatchbo deployments begin in the first quarter of 2027 as planned, if pro forma EBITDA shows the acquired businesses earn their purchase prices, and if the executed agreements show limits that keep distributions and insider payments behind creditors. It would worsen if lease starts slip beyond that quarter, if a large customer uses a termination right, or if the acquired businesses show control weaknesses when they are first tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The customer agreements are not in the documents read, so the finding that concentration is the dominant risk cannot be tested for termination rights, credit support or start dates; longer or better-protected contracts would lower that risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the medium governance rating rests on summaries and cannot separate what the company may do from what it has done; a tight restricted-payment limit would support a lower rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Holder-level ownership and director independence sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the Class B share calculation treats all Class B shares as one block, so the control finding could move once holder figures are known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No pro forma EBITDA is printed for Genco, GESA or Omega, so the finding that share funding limits the leverage added cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Where the quarterly report is silent on the Hatchbo termination right after the July 2026 amendment, the contract durability finding stays open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 transactions were three acquisitions and two senior note issues. Genco, a purchase of leased gas turbines completed on March 16, 2026, cost USD 483.2 million, paid partly with stock issued of USD 238.4 million and financed partly by a USD 300.0 million bridge loan that the May notes repaid; the later report is net of USD 1.1 million recovered from escrow, so the earlier USD 484.3 million is superseded. GESA, completed on July 1, 2026 for USD 263.1 million, included shares of USD 211.5 million and added goodwill of USD 169.5 million; Omega, completed on September 1, 2026 for USD 275.2 million, included shares of USD 178.7 million and added goodwill of USD 110.9 million.

fields.value: The USD 1.3 billion of senior notes due 2031, issued on May 12, 2026, raised net proceeds of USD 1.28 billion and repaid USD 463.9 million of term loans; a USD 650.0 million secured revolver signed the same day was undrawn at September 30, 2026 with USD 125.0 million of letters of credit, and was raised to USD 850.0 million on October 1, 2026. Earlier funding included USD 155.0 million and USD 747.5 million of convertible senior notes, and a Stateline term loan of up to USD 550.0 million, of which USD 408.2 million was drawn at September 30, 2026 without recourse to the company.

fields.value: | 1 | Debt-funded growth ahead of earnings | Total debt reached 2.44 times its year-end 2025 level, USD 2,599.8 million, which is 8.83x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA against 5.97x at FY2025 | Turbines and acquisitions are bought before leases earn rent, so interest and principal come first | Raises default and refinancing risk until lease income arrives | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 2 | Lease starts and customer concentration | No Stateline lease had started by 2026-09-30; one customer was 59% of revenue and 67% of receivables; the first-signed Hatchbo contract could be ended on 30 days notice for 50% of remaining rent | A late start or exit removes rent from the debt that funded the equipment, and the credit agreement can force repayment or cut borrowing if a material contract ends early | Turns a customer event into a liquidity event | Negative | High |

fields.value: | 4 | Interest burden still to come | Annual coupons on the four note issues of USD 179.6 million against reported EBITDA of USD 294.5 million; cash interest cover of 21.08x against 3.55x on total interest cost | Capitalised interest and a late first coupon hide the cost in paid interest | Cover will fall unless new lease earnings arrive | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. (issuer sei-1697500), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is the five supplied SEC filings and the accepted Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance results, in US dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Solaris is a high-risk growth credit: debt more than doubled in nine months to fund equipment that is not yet earning, so creditors depend on a few lease starts arriving on schedule.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation A1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt of USD 2,200.3 million at September 30, 2026 is 7.47x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, and free cash flow over those twelve months was negative USD 1,062.9 million. Support is USD 6,751.5 million of contracted lease payments and open bond markets, which took USD 1.3 billion in May and USD 1.25 billion in October 2026. Pro forma net debt for the October 2026 notes is not established; after a later Stateline draw of USD 25.0 million it is USD 2,225.3 million, or 7.56x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 63

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is high and rising on every measure, and the headline cover ratio flatters. Total debt was 3.29x reported EBITDA at FY2024, 5.97x at FY2025 and 8.83x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, with net leverage at 7.47x, because borrowing for turbines and acquisitions has run ahead of earnings. Cash interest cover of 21.08x is flattered by interest capitalised on assets under construction and by a first coupon on the 2031 senior notes that falls after the period; on total interest cost the nine-month cover is 3.55x, and full-year coupons on the four note issues alone are USD 179.6 million, which last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 294.5 million covers 1.64 times before the Stateline loan, equipment financing and revolver costs. Pro forma net leverage for the October 2026 senior notes is not established, and after the later Stateline draw of USD 25.0 million it is 7.56x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation A11; calculation A12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow is deeply negative and capital markets, not operations, finance the gap. Operating cash flow of USD 573.9 million over the last twelve months includes customer prepayments, with deferred revenue adding USD 207.2 million and contract liabilities USD 77.5 million in the first nine months of 2026, against capital expenditure of USD 1,636.9 million, so free cash flow was negative USD 1,062.9 million. Power equipment purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million remain, USD 569.1 million of them in the rest of 2026, and about USD 1 billion of capital spend is still planned for 2026; the prepayments are interest-free funding that unwinds as leases run, so they do not remove the need for new borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation F24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contracted rent gives revenue visibility, but lease start dates decide when it arrives. Future lease payments of USD 6,751.5 million are disclosed, including leases not yet started, with USD 801.0 million due in 2027 and 50.31% falling after 2030, and 2026 brought several large contracts with affiliates of investment-grade technology companies. No Stateline lease had started by September 30, 2026, the first-signed Hatchbo contract could be ended on 30 days notice for a payment of 50% of remaining rent, and the credit agreement can force repayment or cut borrowing if certain material contracts end early, so a delay or an exit hits liquidity as well as revenue.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 138; calculation A15

fields.value: - Diversification is weak on customers, segment and supplier, and growth is arriving with a thinner margin. One customer was 59% of third-quarter revenue and 67% of receivables, a single data-center customer was 88% of Power Solutions revenue in FY2025, Power Solutions made 75% of revenue and 80% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in nine months, and one supplier was 38% of purchases. Power Solutions Adjusted EBITDA was 59% of its own revenue in nine months 2025 and 52% in nine months 2026.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate for the near term but fell quickly, and the maturity wall is distant. Cash of USD 399.5 million and undrawn revolver of USD 525.0 million gave USD 924.5 million at September 30, 2026, down USD 474.6 million in the quarter from USD 1,399.1 million and covering purchase commitments 0.70 times; the effect on cash of the October 2026 senior notes, with net proceeds of about USD 1.23 billion, is not established. Only USD 209.8 million of principal falls due in 2030 and 85.34% falls due in 2031 or later, and the 2030 convertible notes are in the money, so refinancing is a 2031 question that depends on markets staying open while contracts start.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is growth-first and governance risk is medium. The filings describe no controlling holder and no sponsor extraction: dividends were USD 22.8 million in nine months, 1.65% of capital expenditure, and payments to a company owned by the Chairman were USD 0.8 million, but the company chose debt and shares over deleveraging to fund USD 1,382.4 million of capital expenditure and three acquisitions. Class B holders held about 22% of votes in early 2026, controls at the two acquired services businesses are not yet tested, and the revolver limits net leverage to 5.25x while reported total debt to EBITDA is 8.83x, so the covenant definitions must differ from the reported figures and headroom is not established.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation A19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that reported earnings understate the run rate: GESA and Omega are in results only from July 1 and September 1, 2026, the filing shows pro forma nine-month revenue of USD 1,249.4 million against USD 756.7 million reported, much of the USD 1,382.4 million of capital spend has not yet started earning rent, and the company states compliance with a net leverage limit of 5.25x. Contracted lease payments of USD 801.0 million fall due in 2027 alone, and the largest customers are affiliates of investment-grade technology companies. The view would improve if the Stateline leases start and the Hatchbo deployments begin in the first quarter of 2027 as planned, if pro forma EBITDA and the covenant ratios show leverage well inside the limits, and if the October 2026 notes leave liquidity above commitments. It would worsen if lease starts slip, if a large customer uses a termination right, or if the acquired businesses show control weaknesses when first tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A large contracted lease book supports revenue visibility. Future lease payments of USD 6,751.5 million, including leases not yet started, with USD 801.0 million due in 2027 and 50.31% after 2030, are fixed for the lease term, and the Hatchbo and April 2026 contracts are with affiliates of investment-grade technology companies, so once equipment starts earning, long fixed rent should support debt service; the strength depends on start dates and on termination terms that were not supplied.

fields.value: Demonstrated access to bond, convertible and revolver markets limits near-term refinancing risk. The company issued USD 1.3 billion of senior notes in May and USD 1.25 billion in October 2026 and raised the revolver to USD 850.0 million, and only USD 209.8 million of principal falls due in 2030, so the debt maturity wall sits in 2031 and later; access is proven only in an open market and for a growth story still to be delivered.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy takes little cash out and the filings describe no controlling holder. Dividends of USD 22.8 million and payments of USD 0.8 million to an entity of the Chairman are small against capital expenditure of USD 1,382.4 million, and the filings describe no waiver, exchange offer or priming transaction, so leakage to shareholders is a minor credit risk on current evidence.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; calculation A19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: High and rising leverage is the main weakness. Total debt reached 2.44 times its year-end 2025 level, USD 2,599.8 million, which is 8.83x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, and annual coupons on the four note issues of USD 179.6 million take much of that EBITDA, so earnings from new leases must arrive for coverage to hold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation A1; calculation A11; calculation A12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Negative free cash flow makes the company dependent on outside funding. Operating cash flow of USD 573.9 million, helped by customer prepayments, covered about a third of capital expenditure of USD 1,636.9 million over the last twelve months, and purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million remain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration leaves the credit exposed to one counterparty and one segment. One customer was 59% of revenue and 67% of receivables, Power Solutions was 75% of revenue, and the first-signed Hatchbo contract could be ended on 30 days notice, and if it counts as a material contract under the credit agreement, whose definition was not supplied, its early end could force repayment or reduce borrowing.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 138

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Integration and execution risk has risen with three acquisitions in 2026. GESA and Omega, added on July 1 and September 1, are outside the management assessment of internal control, Omega works mainly under fixed-price contracts, and a new Chief Accounting Officer starts on November 12, 2026, so earnings and reporting could be more volatile than the legacy leasing business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Solaris leases power generation equipment and sells related engineering, construction and operations services to data center, energy and industrial customers, and still builds oilfield proppant-handling equipment. Power Solutions made 75% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026, while Logistics Solutions revenue fell 13% to USD 185.6 million on lower last-mile activity. Lease payments are fixed for the lease term, which gives visibility once equipment is on rent, whereas services and construction revenue is project-based and the oilfield segment follows drilling activity, so cash-flow visibility, and with it debt service and refinancing confidence, depends mainly on how fast contracted leases start.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. is a listed holding company that consolidates the operating company, Solaris Energy Infrastructure, LLC, and Stateline Power, LLC, which it owns 50.1% with the customer holding the rest and whose term loan of USD 408.2 million is non-recourse but counted in group debt. The senior notes are issued by the operating company and guaranteed by the listed company and its restricted subsidiaries, the revolver is secured on substantially all their assets, and the convertible notes are obligations of the listed company that rank behind the senior notes to the extent of the subsidiary guarantees, so creditors of the convertible notes are structurally junior. The filings describe no controlling holder: Class B holders, including Yorktown, the Chairman and legacy sellers of Mobile Energy Rentals, held about 22% of votes in early 2026, and a charter waiver lets designated parties compete and take corporate opportunities, which is a governance weakness without evidence of use.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 42–46; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable once leases start but concentrated, partly cyclical and changing in mix. Leasing revenue rests on contracts of two to fifteen years with extension options, services revenue on project work, and oilfield logistics on drilling and completion activity; one customer was 59% of third-quarter revenue and 67% of receivables, and Power Solutions was 75% of revenue. The credit consequence is that a delay or exit by one counterparty would move cash flow immediately, while the contract book of USD 6,751.5 million supports the long-run level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 69

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended on leases but are thinning as services are added. Power Solutions Adjusted EBITDA was 59% of its revenue in nine months 2025 and 52% in nine months 2026, and its cost of revenue rose to 44% of its revenue from 39%, which fits the addition of GESA and Omega; Omega works predominantly under fixed-price contracts, so cost overruns sit with the company, while the Baker Hughes turbine contract is at a fixed price with only limited escalation. Consolidated reported EBITDA margin was 31.45% over the last twelve months, so lower-margin services appear to dilute the leasing margin and weaken cash conversion per dollar of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 72

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA does not yet convert to free cash flow. Capital expenditure of USD 1,636.9 million over the last twelve months was 2.85 times operating cash flow of USD 573.9 million, and the filings do not split maintenance from growth spending; purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million are cancellable with penalties of 5% to 90% except a non-cancellable USD 364.9 million, so spending can be slowed at a cost but not stopped. Customer prepayments help operating cash flow and unwind as leases run, so free cash flow of negative USD 1,062.9 million shows the recurring gap that new borrowing and shares have filled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation A18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high and supplier power is meaningful. A few large investment-grade customers can negotiate or exit, since the first-signed Hatchbo contract could be ended on 30 days notice for a payment of 50% of remaining rent, and one supplier was 38% of purchases while turbine delivery runs to 2029; the credit effect is pressure on renewal terms and on build timing. Rivalry and substitutes are rising: the filings expect significant competition as distributed power develops and note that distributed power competes with grid access in some uses, so lease renewals after the first term are not assured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Macro and policy factors are not a primary credit driver on the materials read, except through demand: the filings tie demand to data center power needs against constrained grids and list tariffs and trade barriers only as general risks, and no permitting or tariff exposure is quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are contracted lease income, investment-grade counterparties, proven market access and low cash leakage to owners. The weaknesses are high leverage, negative free cash flow, concentration and a thin margin on added services. The opportunities are on-time lease starts and further contract wins, including the larger Hatchbo scope and the October 2026 agreement. The threats are lease delays, a customer termination, covenant or control weaknesses at the acquired businesses and a closed market for refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale is average: revenue of USD 936.4 million over the last twelve months is small against debt of USD 2,599.8 million, and no market-share or peer data was supplied. Competitive advantage is average: integrated services and contracts with investment-grade counterparties help, but termination rights and fixed-price costs limit the moat. Diversification is weak because one customer is 59% of revenue and one supplier 38% of purchases. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because most commitments are cancellable at a penalty but USD 364.9 million is not. Margin stability is average and trending down as Power Solutions margin fell from 59% to 52%. Free cash flow stability is weak, with free cash flow of negative USD 1,062.9 million. Ability to refinance is average: market access has been strong, maturities to 2030 are small, and 85.34% of principal is due in 2031 or later, but leverage is high and no rating was supplied. Liquidity is average: USD 924.5 million of cash and undrawn revolver covers commitments 0.70 times before the October 2026 notes. Financial policy and governance is average, with low cash leakage offset by a growth-first debt policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 58–60; calculation A2; calculation A5; calculation A13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside reported debt add to the constraints: purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million, a Tax Receivable Agreement liability of USD 109.2 million and standby letters of credit of USD 215.6 million. The main supports are contracted rent, market access and low leakage; the main constraints are leverage, cash burn and concentration. The trend is deteriorating on reported measures, with total debt to EBITDA at 3.29x, 5.97x and 8.83x across FY2024, FY2025 and the last twelve months, and the missing data that would most change the picture are pro forma EBITDA, covenant ratios and the terms of the largest customer contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the outlook turns on lease starts. Hatchbo deployments are expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027 and scale through 2028, the April 2026 contract from late 2026 through 2028, and the October 2026 agreement from the first half of 2027, so rent should rise while about USD 1 billion of capital spend is still planned for 2026 and coupons on the senior notes alone reach USD 170.4 million a year. The credit implication is that liquidity and leverage get worse before earnings arrive, and a slip of one quarter would extend the period of negative free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation A10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the filings expect a much larger fleet by the end of 2029, and contracted lease payments run at USD 801.0 million to USD 820.6 million a year from 2027 to 2030 with 50.31% falling after 2030, which supports deleveraging only if costs and tenors hold. The tailwinds are data center power demand against constrained grids and long investment-grade contracts; the headwinds are competition from grid supply and other distributed power, a shrinking oilfield segment and the cost of integrating services businesses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation A15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most credible downside is a delay or loss of a large lease while debt-funded commitments continue. The initiating condition is a late turbine delivery or other delay in making equipment available, since each lease starts only when equipment is ready for the customer, or a customer using its right to end the Hatchbo contract on 30 days notice; the first operational break is equipment that sits idle without rent, as at Stateline where no lease had started by September 30, 2026. Revenue and free cash flow then fall short of plan, while coupons on the senior notes of USD 170.4 million a year, purchase commitments of USD 1,323.9 million and about USD 1 billion of capital spend continue, so liquidity of USD 924.5 million, down USD 474.6 million in one quarter, would be drawn down further before the October 2026 notes are counted. Leverage rises further from 8.83x, the Stateline loan faces its own covenants from the quarter ending March 31, 2027, and the credit agreement can force repayment or cut borrowing if a material contract ends early, which turns a revenue problem into a liquidity problem. Management can cancel purchase commitments at a penalty of 5% to 90%, defer capital spend, stop the dividend of USD 0.12 a share a quarter and issue shares, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress for the next twelve months only if markets stay open; no stress figure is produced because no run-rate earnings or covenant ratios were supplied. The observable triggers are lease commencement dates, revolver availability and any change in the compliance statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sei.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_sei.htm.jsonl, page 138; calculation A10; calculation A4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Solaris presents a business profile that is not fully assessable against peers but is supported by contracted lease income with investment-grade counterparties, proven market access and low cash leakage, and credit quality is constrained by leverage of 8.83x reported EBITDA, negative free cash flow and concentration on a few customers. Cash-flow durability appears weak today and adequate only once leases start, because operating cash flow of USD 573.9 million covers about a third of capital expenditure. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on lease starts on schedule, open convertible and bond markets, and the 2031 wall of 85.34% of principal. The primary downside path is a lease delay or customer exit while debt-funded commitments continue. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, covenant ratios and definitions, the customer contracts and the effect of the October 2026 notes on cash. The monitoring triggers are lease commencement dates, liquidity against commitments, total debt to EBITDA and any change in the covenant compliance statement. Top risk: lease starts slipping or a large contract ending while debt-funded commitments are outstanding.
